questions.solution:
After the vector and the foreign DNA are cut with the same restriction enzyme, their matching sticky ends pair up by hydrogen bonding.

DNA ligase then seals the gaps in the sugar–phosphate backbone by forming phosphodiester bonds, producing a single recombinant DNA molecule; it is called "molecular glue" for this reason.

DNA polymerase builds new strands, gyrase relieves supercoiling and helicase unwinds the helix — none of them joins DNA pieces together.

So the enzyme used is DNA ligase.

questions.text:
Which of the following techniques are used for the transfer of foreign DNA into the host cell?
(A). Microinjection
(B). Shot gun
(C). Ultrasonification
(D). Gel permeation
(E). Electroporation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Microinjection: DNA is injected straight into the nucleus of an animal cell with a fine needle.

Shot gun (gene gun/biolistics): gold or tungsten particles coated with DNA are fired into plant cells at high speed.

Ultrasonification: ultrasound makes temporary pores in the membrane through which DNA enters.

Electroporation: a brief electric pulse opens temporary pores that let DNA in.

Gel permeation is a chromatographic method for separating molecules by size and transfers nothing into cells.

So the transfer techniques are (A), (B), (C) and (E) only.

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements regarding biotechnology.
(A). Exonucleases cut the nucleotides at the ends of DNA strands.
(B). The sequences recognized by restriction enzymes are 4 to 8 nucleotides long.
(C). Baculoviruses are not vectors.
(D). Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a bacterium which can live only in plants.
(E). The bacteria protect their own DNA from nuclease attack by methylating the bases at susceptible sites.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) True: exonucleases remove nucleotides from the free ends of DNA, whereas endonucleases cut within it.

(B) True: restriction enzymes recognise specific (usually palindromic) sites 4–8 base pairs long.

(C) False: baculoviruses are widely used as vectors to express genes in insect cells.

(D) False: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a soil bacterium that infects dicot plants; it is not confined to living in plants.

(E) True: a bacterium's methylase adds methyl groups at its own recognition sites, so its restriction enzyme cannot cut its own DNA.

So the correct statements are (A), (B) and (E) only.

questions.text: Which one of the following palindrome sequence is recognized by restriction enzyme EcoRI?
questions.solution:
A palindromic sequence reads the same on both strands when each is read in the 5′ → 3′ direction.

EcoRI (from E. coli RY13) recognises the six-base sequence 5′ GAATTC 3′, whose complementary strand is 3′ CTTAAG 5′.

It cuts between G and A on each strand, leaving sticky ends with AATT overhangs.

GGATCC is the site of BamHI, GTCGAC of SalI and AGCT of AluI.

So EcoRI recognises 5′ GAATTC 3′ / 3′ CTTAAG 5′.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a technique used for isolation and characterization of macromolecules?
questions.solution:
Macromolecules such as DNA and proteins are separated (isolated) by methods like electrophoresis, gel electrophoresis, chromatography and centrifugation.

They are characterised by methods such as spectroscopy, which studies their interaction with light or radiation.

PCR does not separate or analyse a molecule; it makes many copies of a chosen DNA segment by repeated denaturation, annealing and extension.

So PCR is not a technique for isolation and characterisation of macromolecules.

questions.text:
Which of the following techniques can be used to transfer foreign DNA directly into the cell or protoplasm without the use of plasmids?
(i) Electroporation
(ii) Microinjection
(iii) Lipofection
(iv) Shot gun
(v) Ultrasonification
(vi) Biolistic method
questions.solution:
Vectorless (direct) gene transfer puts DNA into cells or protoplasts without plasmid or viral vectors.

Electroporation uses brief electric pulses to open pores; ultrasonication uses sound waves to make the membrane leaky.

Microinjection delivers DNA straight into the nucleus with a fine glass needle; lipofection carries DNA inside liposomes that fuse with the membrane.

The shot gun (gene gun) or biolistic method fires gold or tungsten particles coated with DNA into the cells.

So all six, (i) to (vi), are direct gene transfer methods.

questions.text: Which of the following is INCORRECT in transformation of rDNA into suitable competent host?
options: The transfer of rDNA into a bacterial cell is assisted by divalent ++ .
The cloning of organisms used in plant biotechnology are E. coli and Agrobacterium tumefaciens.
Host cell takes up naked rDNA by process called transduction.
The host cell which has taken up rDNA called as transformed cell.
questions.solution:
Treating bacteria with divalent Ca2+ ions (then heat shock) makes them competent to take up rDNA, so that statement is true.

E. coli and Agrobacterium tumefaciens are the organisms used for cloning in plant biotechnology, which is also true.

Uptake of naked DNA by a cell is transformation; transduction is gene transfer by a bacteriophage, so that statement is wrong.

A cell that has taken up the rDNA is called a transformed (recombinant) cell, which is true.

So the incorrect statement is the one calling uptake of naked rDNA transduction.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): In rDNA technology, the transformation process generates a mixed population of transformed and non-transformed host cells.
Statement (II): In the screening process, both transformed and non-transformed host cells divide and redivide along with the replication of recombinant DNA.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is true: transformation is inefficient, so only some host cells take up the recombinant DNA, giving a mixture of transformed and untransformed cells.

Statement (II) is false: screening uses a selectable marker (e.g. antibiotic resistance) so that only transformed cells survive and multiply.

The division of host cells along with replication of the recombinant DNA describes amplification of the selected transformed cells, not of both types.

Hence the first statement is right and the second is wrong.

questions.text: The Ti plasmid used in genetic engineering in plants is obtained from -------------.
questions.solution:
Ti stands for tumour-inducing; this plasmid lets the soil bacterium Agrobacterium tumefaciens cause crown gall in dicot plants.

Part of it (T-DNA) is naturally transferred into the plant genome.

After its tumour-causing genes are removed (disarmed), it serves as a vector to carry desired genes into plants.

So the Ti plasmid comes from Agrobacterium tumefaciens.

questions.text: Which of the following technique is used for invitro amplification of gene?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:

✅ Option B – PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)

Explanation:

  • PCR is a molecular biology technique used for in vitro amplification (copying) of a specific gene or DNA segment. It allows the creation of millions of copies of a particular DNA sequence within a few hours.

  • Electrophoresis, PAGE (Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis), and SDS-PAGE are analytical techniques used to separate nucleic acids or proteins based on size and charge — not to amplify them.

Answer: B. PCR

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a technique used for direct transfer of foreign DNA into the protoplast of host cell without using vector?
questions.solution: Gel electrophoresis is used to separate DNA, not to transfer it into protoplasts.

questions.text:
Match the restriction enzyme in Column I with their recognition sequences in Column II.

Choose the correct option:
options: i - d, ii - b, iii - a, iv -c.
questions.solution:
The restriction enzymes and their specific recognition and cleavage sequences are:

(i) AluI recognises and cleaves the blunt-end sequence 5′−↓−3′ (a).

(ii) BamHI recognises and cleaves the sequence 5′−↓−3′ (d).

(iii) EcoRI recognises and cleaves the sequence 5′−↓−3′ (c).

(iv) HindII recognises and cleaves the blunt-end sequence 5′−↓−3′ (b).

Therefore, the correct match is i-a, ii-d, iii-c, iv-b.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: The transfer of rDNA into a bacterial cell for the purpose of its cloning, is assisted by ________ ions.
questions.solution: Ca2+ ions facilitate DNA uptake in bacterial transformation.

questions.text: What is the time duration required for completion of one PCR Cycle?
questions.solution: A PCR cycle (denaturation, annealing, extension) typically takes 3−4 minutes depending on the polymerase and conditions employed.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I - The recognition sites of RENs are 4-8 nucleotides bps long and are characterized by a particular type of internal symmetry.

Statement II - Different restriction enzymes found in different organisms recognise different nucleotide sequences and cut the DNA at different sites.

In the light of above statements, select the correct option given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement I:

The recognition sites of RENs are 4–8 nucleotide base pairs long and are characterized by a particular type of internal symmetry.

✅ This is correct.

Restriction endonucleases (RENs) recognize specific DNA sequences that are typically palindromic—that is, they read the same 5′ → 3′ on both strands. These recognition sequences are usually 4 to 8 base pairs long.

Statement II:

Different restriction enzymes found in different organisms recognise different nucleotide sequences and cut the DNA at different sites.

✅ This is also correct.

Each restriction enzyme has its own specific recognition sequence and cleavage pattern. For example, EcoRI recognizes GAATTC, while HindIII recognizes AAGCTT; both enzymes cut at distinct sites.

✅ Correct Option:

Option A — Both statement I and statement II are correct.

questions.text: In genetic engineering, the foreign DNA is also called ___________ .
questions.solution:
In recombinant DNA technology, the foreign DNA or segment of DNA containing the gene of interest that is joined to a vector (vehicle DNA) for cloning and expression is referred to as passenger DNA.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Match the Column I containing restriction enzymes with Column II containing recognition sequences.
options: i - a ii - d iii - c iv - b
i−b ii - c iii - d iv - a
i - c ii - b iii - d iv - a
i - a ii - c iii - d iv - b
questions.solution:
The recognition sequences and cleavage sites for the given restriction endonucleases are:

1. AluI recognises the 4-base palindromic sequence 5′↓3′ and produces blunt ends, matching (a).
2. BamHI recognises 5′↓3′ and cuts between two guanine residues, matching (d).
3. EcoRI recognises 5′↓3′ and cuts between guanine and adenine, matching (c).
4. HindII recognises 5′↓3′ (a specific 5′3′ sequence) and produces blunt ends, matching (b).

Therefore, the correct combination is i - a, ii - d, iii - c, iv - b.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Which one of the following is considered as molecular scissors in modern biotechnology?
questions.solution:
Option D: Restriction endonucleases

Explanation (NCERT style):

  • Restriction endonucleases are enzymes that can cut DNA at specific sequences.

  • They are called "molecular scissors" because they recognise specific base pair sequences in DNA and cut the DNA at these sites.

  • These enzymes are widely used in genetic engineering to cut and join DNA molecules.

Other options:

  • Reverse transcriptase: Synthesizes DNA from RNA.

  • Taq polymerase: Used in PCR to synthesize DNA.

  • Alkaline phosphatase: Removes phosphate groups from the ends of DNA.

Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option D: Restriction endonucleases

questions.text: The manipulation of genetic material towards a desired end using "in vitro" process is called _________.
questions.solution:
The manipulation of genetic material towards a desired end using "in vitro" process is called genetic engineering.

Correct Option: C. genetic engineering ✅

questions.text: When the phage DNA enters the host bacterium, the host cell protects itself from the viral DNA attacks with the help of _________ enzyme.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:

Option B – restriction endonuclease

Explanation:

  1. When a bacteriophage injects its DNA into the bacterial cell, the host bacterium needs to protect itself from the foreign (viral) DNA.

  2. Bacteria have a defense mechanism in which special enzymes called restriction endonucleases cut the viral DNA at specific recognition sites.

  3. This prevents the viral DNA from multiplying inside the host cell.

  4. Other enzymes given in the options have different functions:

  • Exonuclease: removes nucleotides from the ends of DNA.

  • DNA ligase: joins DNA fragments together.

  • Helicase: unwinds the DNA double helix.

Thus, the bacterial cell uses restriction endonuclease enzymes to protect itself.

questions.text: Agarose gel electrophoresis is used to separate DNA fragments. The DNA fragments separate due to __________ .
options: difference in the base sequence in them
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:

Option D – difference in the size of fragments

Explanation (NCERT method):

  1. DNA fragments are negatively charged because of the phosphate groups.

  2. In agarose gel electrophoresis, these fragments move towards the positive electrode (anode) when an electric current is applied.

  3. The gel acts like a sieve.

  • Smaller DNA fragments can pass more easily through the pores of the gel.

  • Larger DNA fragments move more slowly.

  1. Thus, separation of DNA fragments occurs only because of differences in size (length), not because of their base sequence or staining properties.

Final Answer: DNA fragments separate due to the difference in the size of fragments. ✅

questions.text: The restriction enzymes used as molecular scissors are type of ____________
questions.solution:
1. Restriction enzymes recognise specific DNA sequences and cut the phosphodiester bonds within the DNA backbone.

  2. Enzymes that hydrolyse (break) phosphodiester bonds in nucleic acids are called nucleases.

  3. Nucleases are of two types:

    • Exonucleases – remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA/RNA chains

    • Endonucleases – cut at internal sites of DNA/RNA chains

  4. Restriction enzymes are sequence-specific endonucleases.

Answer: Option B (nucleases)

questions.text: Chimeric DNA is
questions.solution:
Chimeric DNA is recombinant DNA: a single molecule made by joining DNA segments from two different sources, e.g. a foreign gene ligated into a vector.

A gene clone is a set of identical copies of one gene, a transposon is a "jumping gene" that moves from one place in the genome to another, and a shuttle vector is a vector that can replicate in two different host species.

questions.text: In Ti-plasmid, which of the following is removed?
questions.solution:
The Ti (tumour-inducing) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens transfers its T-DNA into plant cells and makes them grow into tumours.

To use it as a cloning vector, its tumour-forming (virulent) genes are removed. The "disarmed" plasmid is no longer pathogenic but can still carry a desired gene into the plant cell, where the gene is expressed.

questions.text: Gene library or DNA library has the collection of
options: Any one type of gene of organism
questions.solution:
A gene library (DNA library) is a collection of cloned DNA pieces of an organism, kept in vectors inside host cells so that they are preserved for later use.

The book takes it to be a collection of cDNA: copy DNA made from the cells' mRNA with reverse transcriptase and then cloned.

It is not a mixture of DNA and RNA, and it holds many genes, not just one type of gene.

questions.text:
Match the following columns and choose the correct option from the codes given below.

Column IColumn II
A.KC Mehta(i)Fluid mosaic model
B.P Maheshwari(ii)First recombinant plasmid
C.Cohen and Boyer(iii)Haploid culture
D.Singer and Nicolson(iv)Rust disease
questions.solution:
K.C. Mehta is known for his work on the rust diseases of wheat, such as black rust caused by Puccinia graminis (A–iv).

P. Maheshwari, India's leading plant embryologist, is linked with haploid (anther) culture, first achieved in his Delhi school (B–iii).

Cohen and Boyer made the first recombinant plasmid by linking an antibiotic-resistance gene to a plasmid and cloned it in E. coli (C–ii).

Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane (D–i).

questions.text: Hairy root disease of dicot plants is caused by
questions.solution:
Hairy root disease of dicots is caused by Agrobacterium rhizogenes; its Ri plasmid makes the infected tissue sprout a mass of hairy roots.

Agrobacterium tumefaciens causes crown gall. Bacillus thuringiensis is a soil bacterium whose toxin is used as a biopesticide against insect pests. Meloidogyne incognita is the root-knot nematode of tobacco, tomato and brinjal.

questions.text: If a recombinant DNA bearing gene for ampicillin resistance is transferred into E. coli cells and the host cells are spread on agar plates containing ampicillin, then
options: both transformed and untransformed recipient cells will die
both transformed and untransformed recipient cells will grow
transformed recipient cells will grow and untransformed recipient cells will die
transformed recipient cells will die and untransformed recipient cells will grow
questions.solution:
The ampicillin-resistance gene acts as a selectable marker. Cells that have taken up the recombinant DNA (transformants) can make the enzyme that inactivates ampicillin, so they grow on the ampicillin plate.

Normal E. coli carries no resistance to ampicillin (or to chloramphenicol, tetracycline or kanamycin), so the untransformed cells are killed. The antibiotic plate thus picks out only the transformed cells.

questions.text: Production of human protein in bacteria by genetic engineering is possible because
options: the human chromosome can replicate in the bacterial cell
the mechanism of gene regulation is identical in humans and bacteria
bacterial cells can carry out RNA splicing reactions
questions.solution:
The genetic code is universal: each codon specifies the same amino acid in bacteria, plants and animals. A human gene placed in a bacterium is therefore read and translated into the same human protein, e.g. human insulin made in E. coli.

Human chromosomes cannot replicate in bacteria, gene regulation differs between prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and bacteria cannot splice introns out of RNA (which is why intron-free cDNA or synthetic genes are used).

questions.text:
Assertion : Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a popular genetic engineer because this bacteria is associated with the roots of all cereal and pulse crops.

Reason : A gene incorporated in the bacterial chromosomal genome gets automatically suppressed into the crop with which the bacteria is associated.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
questions.solution:
Assertion is false: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a "natural genetic engineer" because it transfers a piece of DNA (T-DNA) from its Ti plasmid into the plant genome, causing crown gall tumours. It infects mainly dicots, not the roots of all cereals and pulses; cereals (grasses) are generally not its hosts.

Reason is false: genes are transferred to the plant only from the T-DNA of the Ti plasmid, not from the bacterial chromosome, and nothing is transferred automatically to every associated crop.

questions.text: Biolistic (gene gun) is suitable for
options: constructing recombinant DNA by joining with vectors
questions.solution:
In the biolistic (gene gun) method, microscopic gold or tungsten particles about 1–2 µm across are coated with DNA and shot at high velocity into the target cells.

It is used mainly to transform plant cells, whose cell walls make other methods difficult. It can deliver DNA even into chloroplasts and other organelles.

questions.text:
Assertion : Plasmids are single stranded extrachromosomal DNA.

Reason : Plasmid are usually present in eukaryotic cells.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
questions.solution:
Assertion is false: plasmids are double-stranded, circular, extrachromosomal DNA molecules.

Reason is false: plasmids occur in the cytoplasm of many bacteria and are usually absent from eukaryotic cells.

questions.text: A mixture containing DNA fragments, a,b,c and d , with molecular weights of a+b=c , a>b and d>c , was subjected to agarose gel electrophoresis. The positions of these fragments from cathode to anode sides of the gel would be
questions.solution:
DNA is negatively charged, so in the gel it moves away from the wells at the cathode end towards the anode, and the smaller a fragment, the farther it travels.

Since a+b=c with a>b , fragment c is heavier than both a and b ; and d>c . So d>c>a>b .

Fragment b therefore moves farthest, then a , then c , while d stays nearest the wells. Listed from the farthest band to the one nearest the wells, the order is b,a,c,d .

questions.text: Which of the following DNA sequences qualifies to be designated as a palindrome?
questions.solution:
A palindrome in DNA is a stretch of base pairs that reads the same on both strands when each strand is read in the same direction (5' to 3'). Restriction endonucleases recognise such sequences.

In (d) the upper strand reads 5'–AGCGCT–3', and the lower strand, read from its own 5' end, also reads AGCGCT, so it is a palindrome.

A single strand, as in (a) and (b), cannot qualify, and in (c) the lower strand read 5' to 3' is CTGGTC, which differs from GACGAG.

questions.text: The source of taq polymerase used in PCR is a
questions.solution:
Taq polymerase is a heat-stable DNA polymerase isolated from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus, which lives in hot springs.

It stays active through the high-temperature denaturation step of every PCR cycle, so it need not be added afresh in each cycle.

questions.text:
Assertion : Recognition site should be preferably single and responsive to commonly used restriction enzyme.

Reason : In pBR322 alien DNA is ligated generally in the area of Bam HI site of tetracycline resistance gene.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and reason is correct explanation of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution:
Assertion is true: a cloning vector should have very few, preferably single, recognition sites for the commonly used restriction enzymes; several sites would cut the vector into many fragments and complicate cloning.

Reason is true: in pBR322 foreign DNA is commonly ligated at the BamH I site in the tetracycline resistance gene; the insert inactivates that gene, which helps pick out recombinants.

The Reason is only an example of cloning at such a site; it does not explain why a single site is needed.

questions.text: pBR322, which is frequently used as a vector for cloning gene in E. coli is a/an
questions.solution:
pBR322 is not a naturally occurring plasmid: it was constructed in the laboratory from parts of natural E. coli plasmids, so it is a modified bacterial plasmid.

It carries an origin of replication, two antibiotic-resistance genes (ampicillin and tetracycline) as selectable markers and several unique restriction sites, which makes it a versatile, widely used cloning vector.

questions.text: This method of finding a gene is used when researchers know very little about the gene they are trying to find. This process results in a complete gene library : a collection of copies of DNA fragments that represent the entire genome of an organism.
questions.solution:
In shotgun cloning the DNA of the entire genome is cut into fragments with restriction enzymes, without aiming at any particular gene.

The fragments are inserted into plasmids or viruses and taken into bacteria or yeast; as these hosts multiply they make copies (clones) of every fragment.

The collection of clones is a gene library of the whole genome, which is why the method suits a gene about which little is known. PCR, by contrast, needs primers based on a known sequence.

questions.text:
Assertion : Recoginition site should be preferably single and responsive to commonly used restriction enzyme.

Reason : In pBR 322 alien DNA is ligated generally in the area of Bam-HI site of tetracycline resistance gene.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If both Assertion and Reason are false.
questions.solution:
Assertion is true: the site where alien DNA is inserted should be a single recognition site for a commonly used restriction enzyme, because more than one site would cut the vector into fragments and disturb gene cloning.

Reason is true: in pBR322 foreign DNA is usually ligated at the BamHI site of the tetracycline-resistance gene.

The Reason gives an example of an insertion site; it does not explain why the site must be single.

questions.text:
Assertion : In recombinant DNA technology, human genes are often transferred into bacteria (prokaryotes) or yeast (eukaryote).

Reason : Both bacteria and yeast multiply very fast to form huge population, which express the desired gene.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, then mark (a)
If both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion, then mark (b)
If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false, then mark (c)
If both Assertion and Reason are false statements, then mark (d)
questions.solution:
Assertion is true: human genes such as those for insulin or growth hormone are commonly cloned and expressed in hosts like E. coli or yeast.

Reason is true: these microbes divide very rapidly and are easy to culture, so a single transformed cell soon gives a huge population that makes the desired product in quantity.

This is exactly why they are chosen as hosts, so the Reason explains the Assertion.

questions.text: Plasmids are suitable vectors for gene cloning because
options: these are small circular DNA molecules which can integrate with host chromosomal DNA
these are small circular DNA molecules with their own replication origin site
these can shuttle between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
questions.solution:
Plasmids are small circular extra-chromosomal DNA molecules that replicate on their own, because each has its own origin of replication (ori).

The ori controls how many copies are made, so a gene joined to a plasmid is copied along with it. The copy number can be raised artificially to clone the gene in large amounts.

Antibiotic-resistance genes are useful only as selectable markers. They are not what lets a plasmid carry and multiply a gene.

questions.text: A tumour inducing plasmid widely used in the production of transgenic plant is that of :
questions.solution:
Agrobacterium tumefaciens causes crown gall in dicot plants. Its Ti (tumour-inducing) plasmid has a T-DNA segment that is transferred into the plant cell and integrated into its genome, and vir genes that bring about this transfer.

When the tumour-causing genes of the T-DNA are replaced by a desired gene, the Ti plasmid becomes a vector for producing transgenic plants.

questions.text: Electroporation procedure involves :
options: fast passage of food through sieve pores in phloem elements with the help of electric stimulation
opening of stomatal pores during night by artificial light
making transient pores in the cell membrane to introduce gene constructs
purification of saline water with the help of a membrane system
questions.solution:
In electroporation, a brief pulse of high voltage is applied to cells or protoplasts. It opens temporary pores in the cell membrane through which DNA (gene constructs) in the medium enters the cell, and a small part of it becomes integrated into the genome.

It is one of the methods of introducing recombinant DNA into host cells.

questions.text:
Assertion : In recombinant DNA technology, human genes are often transferred into bacteria (prokaryotes) or yeast (eukaryotes).

Reason : Both bacteria and yeast multiply very fast to form huge population which express the desired gene.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution:
Assertion is true: human genes, such as those for insulin or growth hormone, are routinely cloned and expressed in bacteria like E. coli or in yeast.

Reason is true: these microbes multiply very fast, giving a huge population of cells that all express the inserted gene, so a large amount of the product is obtained.

That is exactly why they are chosen as hosts, so Reason explains Assertion.

questions.text:
Assertion : Agrobacterium tumefaciens is popular in genetic engineering because this bacterium is associated with the roots of all cereal and pulse crops.

Reason : A gene incorporated in the bacterial chromosomal genome-gets automatically transferred to the crop with which the bacterium is associated.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution:
Assertion is false: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a soil bacterium that infects mainly dicot plants, causing crown gall; it is not associated with the roots of all cereals and pulses, and cereals are not its natural hosts. It is popular because it naturally transfers part of its DNA into plant cells.

Reason is false: the gene is transferred from the T-DNA of the Ti plasmid, not from the bacterial chromosome, and it has to be inserted into that T-DNA; nothing passes automatically from the chromosome to the crop.

questions.text: In annealing
options: Taq polymerase adds nucleotides to the annealed primer
questions.solution:
PCR has three steps. In denaturation (about 94∘ ) the two strands separate. In annealing (about 50 - 60∘ ) the primers anneal to the template. In extension, Taq polymerase adds nucleotides to the annealed primers.

Hence annealing is the step in which primers anneal to the DNA template.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Which is also called molecular glue
questions.solution:
DNA ligase joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds between adjacent nucleotides, so it is called molecular glue.

Gyrase relieves supercoiling, helicase unwinds the helix and polymerase synthesises new strands.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Gene transfer is present in
questions.solution:
In biolistics (gene gun), microscopic gold or tungsten particles coated with foreign DNA are shot into plant cells at high velocity, so it is a direct method of gene transfer.

Hybridisation, tissue culture and vegetative propagation do not transfer isolated genes.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Which one of the following is a recognisation site for restriction enzyme Bam HI?
questions.solution:
Bam HI recognises the palindromic sequence 5′−−3′ , whose complementary strand reads 3′−−5′ . A palindrome reads the same in the 5′→3′ direction on both strands. GAATTC is the site of Eco RI, and CCATGG is not complementary to GGATCC .

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which of the following statements is false regarding SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis?
options: SDS is a detergent which gives charge to protein
Large protein move more slowly through gel
SDS is used to maintain the 3-dimentional structure of protein
questions.solution:
In SDS-PAGE, SDS is an anionic detergent that denatures proteins and coats them with a uniform negative charge, so that they separate by size (molecular weight), and larger proteins move more slowly through the gel. SDS destroys the three-dimensional structure instead of maintaining it, so statement D is false.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Given below is a sample of portion of DNA strand given the base sequence on the opposite strand. What is so special show in it? 5’- GAATTC...3’ 3’- CTTAAG ... 5’
questions.solution:
The two strands read 5′3′ and 3′5′ , which is the same sequence in the 5′→3′ direction on both strands. Such a sequence is a palindromic sequence, and this one is the recognition site of EcoRI.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: In recombinant DNA technique, the term vector refers to
options: donor DNA, is identified and picked up through electrophoresis
collection of entire genome in form of plasmid
enzyme, cuts the DNA at specific sites
questions.solution:
A vector is a carrier DNA, such as a plasmid or a virus, that transfers the foreign DNA into a host cell for cloning. The enzyme that cuts DNA is a restriction endonuclease.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The vector for T-DNA is
questions.solution:
The soil bacterium Agrobacterium tumefaciens carries the Ti plasmid, whose T-DNA is transferred into the genome of infected dicot cells, causing crown gall. It is therefore used as the natural vector for T-DNA. Thermus aquaticus is the source of Taq polymerase, and E. coli is the usual host for cloning.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Biolistic technique is used in
questions.solution:
Biolistics (gene gun) bombards cells with high-velocity microparticles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA. It is a method of direct gene transfer into plant cells.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: The thermostable enzymes, Taq and Pfu, isolated from thermophilic bacteria are
questions.solution:
Taq polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus) and Pfu polymerase (from Pyrococcus furiosus) are thermostable DNA polymerases that remain active at the denaturation temperature of PCR.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which of the following is used as a best genetic vector in plants ?
questions.solution:
The Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens transfers its T-DNA into plant cells and is used as the vector for gene transfer in plants. Bacillus thuringiensis supplies the Bt toxin gene, not a vector.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Which one of the following hydrolysis internal phosphodiester bonds in a polynucleotide chain?
questions.solution:
Nucleases cleave phosphodiester bonds of nucleic acids. Endonucleases cut within the polynucleotide chain at internal bonds, while exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends. Lipase and protease act on lipids and proteins.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which one of the following can help in the diagnosis of a genetical disorder?
questions.solution:
PCR amplifies DNA from a few cells, so that gene mutations responsible for genetic disorders can be detected early.

ELISA detects antigens or antibodies in infections, and ABO grouping and NMR do not detect genetic disorders.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Micro-organism which act as a vehicle for foreign gene transfer in higher plants:
questions.solution:
Agrobacterium tumefaciens carries a Ti plasmid whose T-DNA gets integrated into the genome of the infected plant cell. After the tumour-inducing genes are disarmed, the Ti plasmid serves as a vector for delivering foreign genes into dicot plants.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Restriction enzymes are used in genetic engineering, because they
options: can cut DNA at specific base sequence
are nucleases that cut DNA at variable sites
questions.solution:
Restriction endonucleases recognise a specific palindromic base sequence in DNA and cut it at or near that site. This allows the DNA to be cut reproducibly, so that fragments from different sources can be joined. They do not join fragments (ligase does) and do not cut at variable sites.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.solution:
Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites and are basic tools of genetic engineering, so pair D is correct. The central dogma is the flow DNA, RNA, protein and is not tied to the codon alone. Okazaki fragments belong to DNA replication, not splicing. RNA polymerase synthesises RNA from DNA, and an RNA primer is not its product.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: P and Q are required in the extension step of PCR to extend the primer sequences from the 3 ′ end of each primer. Choose the option which correctly fills the blanks P and Q.
questions.solution:
In the extension step of PCR, a thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase, from Thermus aquaticus) extends each primer from its 3′ end using the deoxynucleotides (dNTPs) added to the reaction. A thermolabile enzyme would be denatured at the high temperature of the denaturing step, and ribonucleotides or monophosphates are not the substrates for DNA synthesis.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Vector DNA and foreign DNA are cut by the same restriction enzyme.

Reason (R) : Vector DNA and foreign DNA, cut with same enzyme, produces complimentary sticky ends.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Cutting the vector and the foreign DNA with the same restriction enzyme leaves the same sticky (cohesive) ends on both. These complementary ends base pair, and DNA ligase joins them to form recombinant DNA. Thus the Assertion is true and the Reason is true and explains it.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Significance of heat shock method in bacterial transformation is to facilitate which one of the following steps ?
options: Uptake of DNA through membrane transport proteins
Uptake of DNA through transient pores in the bacterial cell wall
questions.solution:
In bacterial transformation, the cells are made competent with divalent cations such as Ca2+ , incubated with recombinant DNA on ice, given a heat shock at 42∘ for a short time and returned to ice. The heat shock produces transient pores in the cell wall and membrane through which the DNA enters.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Chemically synthesised oligonucleotides are used during annealing in PCR technique.

Reason (R) : The primers bind to the double stranded DNA at their complementary regions.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion: the primers used in annealing are chemically synthesised oligonucleotides, so it is true. Reason: in PCR the double-stranded DNA is first denatured into single strands, and the primers anneal to the complementary regions of these single strands, not to double-stranded DNA. Hence the reason is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which of the following options correctly depicts the recognition site for EcoRI ?
questions.solution:
EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence

5′3′3′5′

It cuts each strand between G and A, a little away from the centre of the palindrome, so that single-stranded sticky ends with the overhang AATT are left on both fragments.

Option (D) shows the sequence GAATTC/CTTAAG with the cut between G and A on the upper strand and between A and G (that is, between G and A read from 5′ to 3′ ) on the lower strand.

Option (A) has the correct sequence but cuts at its centre, which would give blunt ends; options (B) and (C) show the sequence GTCGAC, which is not the EcoRI site.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Match Column-I with Column-II and choose the correct option :

Column-IColumn-II
a. Biolistic guni. Bacterial cell
b. Chitinaseii. Tumour inducing
c. Tiiii. Animal cell
d. Ca++iv. Fungal cell
v. Plant cell

Options :
options: a – i, b – ii, c – iii, d – iv
a – ii, b – v, c – i, d – iii
a – v, b – iv, c – ii, d – i
a – v, b – i, c – iv, d – ii
questions.solution:
A biolistic (gene) gun is used to introduce DNA into plant cells, so a matches v.

Chitinase digests chitin of the fungal cell wall when protoplasts are isolated, so b matches iv.

Ti is the tumour-inducing plasmid of Agrobacterium, so c matches ii.

Ca 2+ makes bacterial cells competent to take up DNA, so d matches i.

Thus a-v, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which of the following statements about plasmids is incorrect ?
options: Plasmids have the ability to replicate within the bacterial cell.
Their replication is controlled by chromosomal DNA.
They are autonomously replicating circular extra-chromosomal DNA.
questions.solution:
Plasmids are autonomously replicating, circular, extra-chromosomal DNA molecules, and they often carry antibiotic resistance genes. They replicate within the bacterial cell on their own origin of replication, independent of chromosomal DNA.

Hence the statement that their replication is controlled by chromosomal DNA is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a component required for Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) ?
questions.solution:
PCR needs template DNA to be amplified, two primers to initiate synthesis, nucleotides, and a thermostable DNA polymerase (such as Taq polymerase) to extend the primers.

DNA ligase joins DNA fragments in the cloning step; it is not required in PCR.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Expression of a particular gene helps to identify transformants. What is this gene known as ?
questions.solution:
A gene whose expression helps to identify and select the transformed cells (transformants) from non-transformants is called a selectable marker, for example an antibiotic-resistance gene.

A plasmid is the vector, a structural gene codes for a protein, and an intron is a non-coding part of a gene.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: To separate repetitive DNA from bulk genomic DNA, which of the following method is used ?
questions.solution:
Repetitive DNA has a base composition different from the bulk genomic DNA, so on density gradient centrifugation it forms a separate peak, called a satellite DNA band, at a different density.

Elution recovers DNA from a gel, Southern blotting detects a specific sequence by hybridisation, and PCR amplifies a chosen segment; none of them separates bulk DNA from repetitive DNA.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Which of the following is used to visualize DNA bands under UV light after gel electrophoresis ?
questions.solution:
After gel electrophoresis the DNA fragments are stained with ethidium bromide, which intercalates into DNA. Exposure to UV light makes the DNA bands appear as bright orange colour. Acetocarmine stains chromosomes, safranin stains lignified tissue, and potassium iodide does not stain DNA.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : DNA Ligase is used to join DNA fragments.

Reason (R) : It catalyses the formation of glycosidic bonds between nucleotides.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not correct explanation for Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
DNA ligase seals nicks and joins DNA fragments, so Assertion (A) is true.

It does so by catalysing the formation of phosphodiester bonds between the 3′-OH and 5′-phosphate of adjacent nucleotides, not glycosidic bonds (which link a base to a sugar). Reason (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Match Column I with Column II and select the correct option :

Column IColumn II
a. Primersi. β-galactosidase
b. Insertional inactivationii. To separate and purify products
c. Bioreactoriii. Chemically synthesized oligonucleotides
d. Downstream processingiv. Large scale production of specific product of activity of microbes

Options :
questions.solution:
Primers are short chemically synthesised oligonucleotides, used in PCR (a-iii).

Insertional inactivation of the gene for β -galactosidase in the vector is used to select recombinants (b-i).

A bioreactor is used for large-scale production of a specific product through the activity of microbes (c-iv).

Downstream processing is the separation and purification of the products (d-ii).

Thus a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : DNA cannot pass through cell membrane of a bacterial cell.

Reason (R) : DNA is a hydrophilic molecule.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
DNA is a large, charged (negatively charged phosphate backbone), hydrophilic molecule, so it cannot cross the hydrophobic lipid bilayer of the cell membrane. Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and the hydrophilic nature is the reason DNA cannot pass through.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: What does I in restriction enzyme Hind S2I indicate ?
options: It cuts after the first nucleotide in the restriction site.
It is the first enzyme isolated from strain S2 of bacterium.
Only one enzyme can be used to digest a plasmid from S2 strain.
Only one restriction enzyme has been isolated from this bacteria.
questions.solution:
Restriction enzymes are named by the genus initial, the first two letters of the species, the strain, and a roman numeral. Here, Hin is from Haemophilus influenzae, 2 is the strain (Rd), and the roman numeral I shows the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain.

Hence, I indicates that it is the first enzyme isolated from strain 2 of the bacterium.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Elution means :
options: making the DNA bands visible under UV radiations.
separation of DNA fragments on agarose gel.
isolating alien DNA from the choice organism.
cutting and extraction of DNA bands from the agarose gel.
questions.solution:
Elution is the cutting out of the separated DNA bands from the agarose gel and their extraction from the gel piece, so that the purified fragments can be used for cloning.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: The construction of the first recombinant DNA was done by using the native plasmid of :
questions.solution:
The first recombinant DNA was constructed by Cohen and Boyer in 1972. They joined an antibiotic resistance gene from the native plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium into a plasmid of E. coli.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: In pBR322, tetracycline, resistance gene (tetR) has recognition site for which of the following restriction endonuclease ?
questions.solution:
In the cloning vector pBR322, the tetracycline resistance gene ( tetR ) carries the recognition sites of BamH I, Sal I and Sph I, whereas Pst I and Pvu I lie in the ampR gene.

Cloning a foreign DNA at the BamH I site inactivates tetR , so recombinants lose tetracycline resistance. EcoR I lies outside both resistance genes and Pst I lies in ampR .

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The use of chitinase enzyme is necessary for the separation of DNA from yeast cells but not in the case of Spirogyra.

Reason (R) : Fungal cell wall is made up of fungal chitin.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Fungal cell walls are made up of chitin, so chitinase must be used to digest the wall of yeast (a fungus) to release its DNA, which makes Reason (R) true.

Spirogyra is an alga whose cell wall is made of cellulose, so chitinase is not needed and cellulase is used instead; Assertion (A) is true and R explains it.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Given below is the restriction site of a restriction endonuclease Pst I and the cleavage sites on a DNA molecule.

Choose the option that gives the correct resultant fragments.
options:
5′ C – T – G C – A – G 3′
3′ G – A – C – G – T C 5′

5′ C – T G – C – A – G 3′
3′ G – A – C – G T – C 5′

5′ C – T – G – C A – G 3′
3′ G – A – C – G T – C 5′

5′ C – T – G – C – A G 3′
3′ G A – C – G – T – C 5′
questions.solution:
Pst I recognises the palindromic sequence 5′3′ , which reads the same on both strands in the 5′→3′ direction, and cuts each strand between A and G, as the arrows show.

The upper strand is cut between A and G, giving 5′ and 3′ .

The lower strand, 3′5′ , is cut between G and A, giving 3′ and 5′ .

Therefore the left fragment carries 5′ paired with 3′ , and the right fragment carries 3′ paired with 5′ , each with a single-stranded sticky end of four bases.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Isolation of DNA from a bacterial cell can be achieved by using :
questions.solution:
A bacterial cell is enclosed by a cell wall made of peptidoglycan, which must be broken to release DNA. Lysozyme digests this wall. Cellulase acts on plant cell walls, protease degrades proteins and ribonuclease degrades RNA.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
During gel electrophoresis migration of DNA fragments leading to their separation takes place on the agarose gel.

Choose the correct option :
options: The smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves.
Positively charged fragments moves to farther end.
The larger the fragment size, the farther it moves.
The negatively charged fragments do not move.
questions.solution:
DNA is negatively charged, so in gel electrophoresis the fragments move towards the anode (positive electrode) through the agarose gel.

The gel acts as a sieve, so smaller fragments move faster and farther than larger ones.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : In bioreactors, raw materials are biologically converted into desired products.

Reason (R) : In bioreactors, optimum growth conditions for microbes such as temperature, pH, substrate, salts, etc. are available.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
A bioreactor is a vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, so the assertion is true. It provides optimum conditions such as temperature, pH, substrate and salts for the growth of the microbes, so the reason is true and is the explanation of how the conversion is achieved.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Identify the material that helps in the precipitation of purified DNA during the process of isolation of DNA as shown in the given diagram.
questions.solution:
During isolation of DNA, the cell wall is broken by enzymes such as lysozyme (bacteria) or cellulase (plant cells), and RNA and proteins are removed by ribonuclease and protease.

The purified DNA finally precipitates out on addition of chilled ethanol. It appears as a collection of fine threads in the suspension, which can be spooled out on a hook or glass rod, as shown in the diagram.

Protease, lysozyme and cellulase act at earlier steps and do not precipitate DNA.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: What is the process of binding a primer to the denatured strand called ?
questions.solution:
Each cycle of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) has three steps: denaturation, annealing and extension.

In denaturation, the double-stranded DNA is heated to a high temperature (about 94∘ ) so that its two strands separate. On cooling, the two primers bind to their complementary sequences at the 3′ ends of the single-stranded templates; this step is called annealing, as shown in the diagram.

Thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) then extends the primers, which is the extension (polymerisation) step.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The enzyme ‘Taq Polymerase’ used in PCR, has been isolated from bacterium :
questions.solution:
PCR needs a DNA polymerase that remains active during the repeated high-temperature denaturation steps (about 94∘ ).

Taq polymerase is such a thermostable enzyme, isolated from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus.

Agrobacterium tumefaciens is the source of the Ti plasmid, Streptomyces albus of the restriction enzyme SalI and Escherichia coli of EcoRI and ligase, none of which is the source of Taq polymerase.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Amplification of gene of interest by using DNA polymerase may go upto
questions.solution:
In PCR, each cycle of denaturation, primer annealing and extension by the thermostable DNA polymerase doubles the number of copies of the DNA.

Repeated cycles therefore amplify the gene of interest exponentially, up to about a billion times.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : A bioreactor provides the optimal conditions for achieving the desired product by providing optimum growth conditions.

Reason (R) : The most commonly used bioreactors are of stirring type.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
A bioreactor provides optimal growth conditions such as temperature, pH, substrate and oxygen, which give the desired product in large quantity, so the assertion is true.

The stirring-type bioreactor is the most commonly used type, so the reason is also true.

The reason describes only the type of reactor in common use and does not explain how the optimal conditions are provided, so it is not the correct explanation.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Select the correct statement from the following biotechnological procedures :
options: The polymerase enzyme joins the gene of interest and the vector DNA.
Gel electrophoresis is used for amplification of a DNA segment.
PCR is used for isolation and separation of gene of interest.
Plasmid DNA acts as vector to transfer the piece of DNA attached to it.
questions.solution:
A plasmid is a small circular DNA that replicates independently in a host, so the piece of DNA attached to it is carried into the host cell. Statement (D) is correct.

DNA ligase, not polymerase, joins the gene of interest to the vector; gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments by size and does not amplify them; PCR amplifies a DNA segment and does not isolate or separate it.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Restriction endonuclease recognises palindromic sequence in DNA and cuts them.

Reason (R) : Palindromic sequence has two unique recognition sites PstI and PvuI recognised by restriction endonuclease.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
A restriction endonuclease recognises a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in DNA, one that reads the same in the 5′→3′ direction on both strands, and cuts the strands at that site. The Assertion is true.

PstI and PvuI are themselves restriction enzymes, and each recognises its own different palindromic sequence. A palindromic sequence does not contain recognition sites for them, so the Reason is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Meristematic cells (apical and axillary meristems) are free of virus, so meristem culture in vitro gives virus-free plants. Hence the Assertion is true.

The Reason is false, because a virus-infected plant carries the virus in roots and stems as well, through its vascular tissue. The apical meristem is free because it has no vascular system.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Isolation of DNA from a fungal cell can be achieved by using :
questions.solution:
The fungal cell wall is made of chitin, so chitinase digests it to release DNA. Cellulase acts on plant cell walls, lysozyme on bacterial cell walls, and protease breaks down proteins.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: pBR which is frequently used as a vector for cloning gene in E. coli is a/an :
questions.solution:
pBR322 is a plasmid vector which does not occur naturally. It was engineered from natural bacterial plasmids to carry two antibiotic resistance genes and a unique set of cloning sites (ori, amp R , tet R and a rop gene).

It is therefore a modified bacterial plasmid, not an original plasmid, a viral genome or a transposon.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement regarding PCR.
options: Two sets of primers are required during polymerisation.
The process of replication is repeated multiple times to produce one billion copies.
Thermostable DNA polymerase is used for extension of primers.
Annealing is required to separate both the strands of template DNA.
questions.solution:
In PCR, the strands of the template DNA are separated by denaturation at high temperature, not by annealing. Annealing is the binding of the primers to the separated strands.

The other statements are correct: two sets of primers are needed, Taq polymerase is thermostable and extends the primers, and repeated cycles give about a billion copies.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: The cloning site present in the ampicillin resistance gene of E. coli cloning vector pBR322 is :
questions.solution:
In pBR322 the ampicillin resistance gene (amp R ) carries the recognition site of Pst I (and Pvu I), whereas BamH I and Sal I lie in the tetracycline resistance gene (tet R ). EcoR I lies outside both resistance genes.

Insertion of alien DNA at the Pst I site inactivates ampicillin resistance, which is used for selecting recombinants.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: The cloning site present in the rop site of E. coli cloning vector pBR322 is :
questions.solution:
The vector pBR322 has the genes R and R as selectable markers, the ori and the rop gene, which codes for proteins that control plasmid copy number.

The cloning site Pvu II lies within the rop region, whereas Pst I (and Pvu I) lies in R , and BamH I (and Sal I) lies in R . EcoR I lies outside these genes.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: The cloning site present in the tetracycline resistance gene of E. coli cloning vector pBR322 is :
questions.solution:
In the cloning vector pBR322, the tetracycline resistance gene (tet R ) carries recognition sites for restriction enzymes such as Sal I and BamH I. Pst I (and Pvu I) lie in the ampicillin resistance gene, while EcoR I and Pvu II lie outside the two resistance genes, so only Sal I among the options lies in the tetracycline gene.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Isolation of DNA from a plant cell can be achieved by using :
questions.solution:
The cell wall of a plant cell is mainly cellulose, so cellulase is used to digest it and release the DNA. Lysozyme acts on bacterial cell walls and chitinase on fungal cell walls.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which one of the following enzymes a fungal cell should be treated with to get the DNA along with other macro molecules released from it ?
questions.solution:
The cell wall of fungi is made of chitin, so a fungal cell must be treated with chitinase to break the wall and release the DNA along with other macromolecules. Cellulase acts on plant cells, and ribonuclease only removes RNA.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Which of the following is not required for PCR ?
questions.solution:
PCR needs the DNA segment to be amplified, two primers, the four deoxynucleotides, and the thermostable Taq polymerase.

Restriction endonuclease is used to cut DNA in cloning but is not needed in PCR.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : In genetic engineering, antibiotic genes are used as selectable markers.

Reason (R) : Selectable markers help us to identify transformants from non-transformants.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
A selectable marker, such as an antibiotic-resistance gene, lets only transformed cells grow on a medium containing the antibiotic, so transformants are distinguished from non-transformants. The Assertion and the Reason are both true, and the Reason explains the Assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: The sequence that controls the copy number of linked DNA in the vector is termed :
questions.solution:
The origin of replication (ori) is the sequence from where replication starts, and any DNA linked to it is also replicated in the host cell. The ori site therefore controls the copy number of the linked DNA.

A selectable marker identifies transformants, a palindromic sequence is the site cut by a restriction enzyme, and a recognition site is where the enzyme binds; none of these controls copy number.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Restriction Endonuclease – Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of :
questions.solution:
Restriction endonucleases recognise a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in DNA and cut the strands at a fixed point within or near it. Hind II was the first restriction endonuclease isolated, and it always cuts DNA by recognising a specific sequence of six base pairs.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several monocot plants.

Reason (R) : It is able to deliver a piece of DNA known as ‘T-DNA’ to transform normal plant cells into a tumor.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of many dicot plants and not of monocots, so Assertion (A) is false. It delivers a piece of DNA called T-DNA that transforms normal plant cells into tumour cells, so Reason (R) is true.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Using a DNA template, how many new DNA molecules would be generated after 10 cycles of amplification in PCR ?
questions.solution:
In PCR each cycle (denaturation, annealing, extension) doubles the number of DNA molecules.

After n cycles, the number of copies from one template is 2n .

For n=10 , 210=1024 .

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Which one of the following bacteria were used by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer to accomplish the construction of the first rDNA ?
questions.solution:
The first recombinant DNA was constructed by linking a gene encoding antibiotic resistance with a native plasmid (an autonomously replicating, circular, extra-chromosomal DNA) of Salmonella typhimurium.

In 1972, Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer cut out the piece of DNA carrying the antibiotic-resistance gene with a restriction enzyme and joined it to the cut plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium using DNA ligase, giving the first rDNA.

This rDNA was afterwards transferred into E. coli, a closely related bacterium, where it replicated; E. coli served only as the host. Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a natural vector of plant cells, and Mycobacterium was not involved.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a feature of plasmids ?
questions.solution:
Plasmids are extra-chromosomal, self-replicating, double-stranded circular DNA molecules in bacteria. Being single stranded is therefore not a feature of plasmids.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Specific enzymes are used to degrade the cell wall in organisms to isolate the DNA from the cell.

Reason (R) : Fungal cell wall is degraded by the enzyme cellulase.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
To isolate DNA, the cell wall must be broken open with specific enzymes: lysozyme for bacteria, cellulase for plant cells and chitinase for fungi. Hence Assertion (A) is true.

The fungal cell wall is made of chitin, not cellulose, so it is degraded by chitinase and not by cellulase. Hence Reason (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which one of the following is not used as a vector for rDNA technology ?
questions.solution:
A vector carries the foreign DNA into a host and is used to clone it. Plasmids, bacteriophages and retroviruses are used as cloning vectors.

A bacterial cell is the host in which the recombinant DNA is propagated, and is not a vector.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : A recombinant DNA which is inserted within the coding sequence of β -galactosidase does not produce blue coloured colonies when treated with a chromogenic substrate.

Reason (R) : Insertional inactivation occurs when a recombinant DNA is introduced in the coding sequence of the enzyme.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
When a recombinant DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of β -galactosidase, the enzyme is inactivated; this is insertional inactivation. The bacterial colonies then cannot convert the chromogenic substrate into the blue product, so they appear colourless. Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Which native plasmid did Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer use for the construction of the first recombinant DNA ?
questions.solution:
Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer in 1972 isolated an antibiotic resistance gene from a plasmid of the bacterium Salmonella typhimurium and linked it with a native plasmid of the same bacterium, to construct the first recombinant DNA.

The other bacteria listed were not the source of this plasmid.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A): The stirrer facilitates the even mixing of oxygen availability in a bioreactor.

Reason (R): Stirred-tank bioreactors generally have a flat base.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The stirrer of a stirred-tank bioreactor mixes the contents evenly and distributes oxygen throughout the culture, so Assertion (A) is true.

Stirred-tank bioreactors have a curved base, which helps the contents mix properly, rather than a flat base. Reason (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which one of the following represents the correct annealing of primers to the DNA to be amplified in the PCR ?
questions.solution:
A primer is a short single-stranded oligonucleotide that base-pairs with its template strand in the antiparallel orientation. DNA polymerase extends it only from its free 3′ -OH end, so each primer must anneal at the 3′ end of its template strand with its own 3′ end pointing into the region to be amplified.

In (B), the upper template runs 5′→3′ from left to right and its primer sits at the right-hand ( 3′ ) end as 3′ – 5′ ; the lower template runs 3′→5′ and its primer sits at the left-hand ( 3′ ) end as 5′ – 3′ . Both primers are antiparallel to their templates and their 3′ ends face each other across the target, so extension copies the DNA between them.

In (A), (C) and (D), every primer runs parallel to its template strand, so it cannot pair and be extended correctly.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: For the replication of the first recombinant DNA, Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer used the DNA polymerase of :
questions.solution:
Cohen and Boyer in 1972 constructed the first recombinant DNA by linking an antibiotic resistance gene with a plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium and propagated it in Escherichia coli, using the host's DNA polymerase for replication.

Thermus aquaticus is the source of Taq polymerase used in PCR, not of the enzyme used in this work.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: The linking of the antibiotic resistance gene with the plasmid vector of Salmonella typhimurium by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer was made possible by the enzyme :
questions.solution:
Restriction endonuclease cut the plasmid and the antibiotic resistance gene, and DNA ligase joined the two to form the recombinant DNA.

Hence the linking was made possible by DNA ligase.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: The ‘molecular scissors’ fall in the category of :
questions.solution:
The molecular scissors are restriction enzymes, which cut DNA at specific recognition sequences. Restriction enzymes are a particular kind of restriction endonuclease that cuts at, or near, a specific sequence, whereas a general endonuclease or exonuclease does not recognise a specific site. The category is therefore restriction enzymes.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Plasmids are autonomously replicating circular extra-chromosomal DNA.

Reason (R) : Plasmids are usually present in Eukaryotic cells.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Plasmids are autonomously replicating, circular, extra-chromosomal DNA, so Assertion (A) is true.

Plasmids are usually present in bacterial cells, not in eukaryotic cells (yeast is a rare exception). Reason (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is correct in the context of observing DNA separation by agarose gel electrophoresis ?
options: DNA can be seen in visible light.
DNA can be seen without staining in visible light.
Ethidium bromide stained DNA can be seen in visible light
Ethidium bromide stained DNA can be seen under UV light.
questions.solution:
DNA fragments separated on an agarose gel are invisible in visible light. They are stained with ethidium bromide, and the stained DNA appears as orange-coloured bands when exposed to UV light.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Given below are two columns. In Column I is the list of four enzymes and in Column II is the list of functions of the given enzymes. Which one of the following options shows the enzymes matched with their respective functions correctly ?

Column I (Enzyme)Column II (Function)
P.DNA Ligasei.Removes nucleotides from ends of DNA
Q.Restriction exonucleaseii.Extends primer on a DNA template
R.Taq polymeraseiii.Joins the DNA fragments
S.Restriction endonucleaseiv.Cuts DNA at a specific position

Options :
questions.solution:
DNA ligase joins DNA fragments, so P matches iii.

Restriction exonuclease removes nucleotides from the ends of DNA, so Q matches i.

Taq polymerase extends the primer on a DNA template during PCR, so R matches ii.

Restriction endonuclease cuts DNA at a specific position within the molecule, so S matches iv.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: The organism used in construction of the first artificial recombinant DNA by Cohen and Boyer in 1972 was :
questions.solution:
Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer in 1972 made the first recombinant DNA by joining a gene for antibiotic resistance to a native plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium, using a restriction enzyme and DNA ligase. The recombinant plasmid was then introduced into E. coli, where it replicated.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Given below are the steps carried out to construct a recombinant DNA. Which one of the following gives the correct sequence of these steps ?

(i) Isolation of genetic material

(ii) Insertion of recombinant DNA in the host cell / organism

(iii) Obtaining the foreign gene product

(iv) Amplification of gene of interest

(v) Downstream processing
questions.solution:
The steps of recombinant DNA technology are isolation of the genetic material, amplification of the gene of interest by PCR, insertion of the recombinant DNA into the host, obtaining the foreign gene product and finally downstream processing.

Therefore the order is (i) → (iv) → (ii) → (iii) → (v).

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
After the completion of biosynthetic stage in a bioreactor, the product undergoes a series of processes before it is ready for marketing.

List of the processes is given below. Identify the option that gives the correct sequence of the processes carried out :

(i) Purification of product

(ii) Formulation with suitable preservative

(iii) Separation of product

(iv) Clinical trial of product
questions.solution:
After the biosynthetic stage the product is first separated, then purified, then formulated with a suitable preservative, and finally put through clinical trials before marketing.

Therefore the order is (iii) → (i) → (ii) → (iv).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Which of the following samples of DNA in the table given below will give the desired result during polymerase chain reaction ?

SampleTemperature used for DenaturationEnzyme used for extension
(a)IHigh temp. / 90°CHeat stable
(b)IILow temp. / 50°CHeat stable
(c)IIILow temp. / 50°CHeat resistant
(d)IVHigh temp. / 90°CHeat unstable
questions.solution:
In PCR the double-stranded template is first denatured at a high temperature (about 9095∘ ), which separates the two strands. At 50 °C the strands would not separate.

The extension step needs an enzyme that survives this heating, i.e. a heat-stable polymerase (Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus). A heat-unstable enzyme would be denatured during the cycles.

Only sample I combines high-temperature denaturation with a heat-stable enzyme.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : In order to cut the DNA with a restriction enzyme, it needs to be released from the membrane which encloses it.

Reason (R) : A plant cell was treated with chitinase to achieve this.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion: a restriction enzyme can cut DNA only after the DNA is released from the cell, i.e. after the cell membrane and nuclear envelope are broken down, so the assertion is true.

Reason: the cell wall of a plant cell is made of cellulose, which is digested by cellulase. Chitinase is used for the chitin wall of fungi, so the reason is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A): Synthetic oligonucleotide polymers are used during Annealing in a PCR.

Reason (R): The primers bind to the double stranded DNA at their complementary regions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
In PCR, the annealing step uses two synthetic oligonucleotides (primers), so (A) is true.

Annealing follows denaturation, so the template is single-stranded at this stage. The primers bind to their complementary regions on the separated single strands, not on double-stranded DNA, so (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Given below is the restriction site of a restriction endonuclease Pst-I and the cleavage sites on a DNA molecule.

Choose the option that gives the correct resultant fragments by the action of the enzyme Pst-I.
questions.solution:
Pst-I recognises the palindromic sequence 5′3′ and cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone of each strand between A and G, as marked by the arrows. On the upper strand the cut falls after 5′C−T−G−C−A , and on the lower strand, read 3′→5′ , it falls after the first base G .

The two cuts are staggered, so the left fragment carries 5′C−T−G−C−A on the upper strand paired with only 3′G on the lower strand, while the right fragment carries G3′ on the upper strand paired with A−C−G−T−C5′ on the lower strand. Each fragment thus has a single-stranded overhang (sticky end), and the bases of both strands remain unchanged.

Options (A) and (C) cut the strands at positions other than the marked sites, and option (B) also alters the base sequence of the lower strand.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
The given schematic illustration shows three steps ‘P’, ‘Q’ and ‘R’ of the polymerase chain reaction.

Which of the following statements are correct with reference to the illustration given above ?

(i) Step ‘P’ is showing denaturation at low temperature.

(ii) Step ‘Q’ is a denaturation of DNA strand at high temperature, followed by annealing.

(iii) Step ‘R’ is an extension of DNA in presence of thermostable DNA polymerase.

(iv) Step ‘Q’ is extension with two sets of primers.
questions.solution:
In the illustration, step P is the double-stranded template DNA carrying the target region (hatched), step Q shows the two strands separated with a short primer bound to each, and step R shows both primers lengthened into two new double-stranded copies of the target region.

Statement (i) is incorrect: the strands are separated (denatured) by heating to a high temperature (about 94∘ ), not a low one.

Statement (ii) is correct: the template is first denatured at high temperature and, on cooling, the two primers anneal to their complementary sequences on the separated strands, as seen in step Q.

Statement (iii) is correct: in step R the primers are extended by a thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus), which stays active at the high temperatures used in each cycle.

Statement (iv) is incorrect: step Q shows annealing of the primers; extension occurs only in step R.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
